landing.title: Devgame
landing.tagline: A roguelike whose dungeon is a Git graph.
landing.pitch: You work on a project that never ends, one commit at a time. At every node there are two ways forward: by hand, slow and safe, or with the AI, fast and risky. Whatever ships to production unread eventually breaks something there.
landing.howItWorks1: Pick a profile, then walk the graph node by node.
landing.howItWorks2: Every commit is a bet, and the odds are shown before you take it.
landing.howItWorks3: Ship without breaking production for long enough, or leave before it does.
landing.dailySeed: In daily seed mode everyone plays the same map, every UTC day.
landing.metaDescription: A free browser roguelike where the dungeon is a Git graph. Commit by hand or let the machine do it, repay your technical debt, and ship without breaking production.
landing.ogSubtitle: A roguelike whose dungeon is a Git graph
landing.keywords: roguelike, browser game, git, developer game, management game, daily seed, free game
landing.headline: The dungeon is a Git graph. You are not the only developer on it.
landing.ctaNote: Free, no account to start, nothing to install.
landing.pillarCraft: Slow and expensive in energy, but it almost always lands and it leaves nothing behind.
landing.pillarAi: Three times the ground for a third of the cost, and a technical debt you only ever see roughly.
landing.pillarDebt: It grows with every commit the machine writes, it drags every roll down, and it ends up in production.
landing.honestTitle: What this is, and what it is not
landing.honest: A personal project: free, no advertising, no tracking. Scores are verified by replaying the run on the server, so the leaderboard means something. The game runs offline in your browser; an account only exists to carry your progress to another machine and to put you on the board.

notice.title: Legal notice
notice.description: Publisher, host, intellectual property and contact details for Devgame.
notice.hostIntro: The site runs in a container, on a single virtual private server, at:
notice.ipP1: The game's code, rules, text and artwork belong to the publisher unless stated otherwise. Copying or reusing them requires written permission.
notice.ipP2: The site is set in JetBrains Mono, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and builds on open-source libraries, each under its own licence.
notice.reportP1: Content you believe to be unlawful — an abusive display name on the leaderboard, for instance — can be reported to the contact address above. The publisher takes it down if it is.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What the site stores, why, and how to have it erased.
privacy.summaryI1: No analytics, no advertising, no tracker, no third-party embed.
privacy.summaryI2: Signed out, nothing leaves your browser.
privacy.summaryI3: Signed in: your email address, your progress and your runs.
privacy.summaryI4: The only cookie is your session cookie.
privacy.controllerP1: The controller is the site's publisher, identified in the legal notice.
privacy.offlineP1: The game works offline. Your progress and the run in progress are written to your browser's local storage, under the keys devgame:meta:v1, devgame:run:v1 and devgame:pending-submit:v1.
privacy.offlineP2: Nothing is sent to the server until you sign in. Clearing the site's data erases all of it, for good: the publisher holds no copy.
privacy.accountP1: You sign in through a link sent to your email address and, when the publisher has configured it, through Google. Both routes prove the same thing — that the address is yours — so both lead to the same account.
privacy.accountI1: Account: id, name, email address, a verified-address flag, and an avatar URL when it comes from Google.
privacy.accountI2: Sessions: a token, its expiry date, and the IP address and browser used to open the session.
privacy.accountI3: External sign-in: your Google account identifiers and the matching OAuth tokens, only if you go through Google.
privacy.accountI4: Verification: the sign-in tokens emailed to you, valid for fifteen minutes.
privacy.accountP2: Legal basis: performing the service you asked for. The email address is required — it is what identifies the account.
privacy.gameP1: Your profile: display name, level, XP, banked commits, lifetime commits, tickets delivered, unlocks and settings.
privacy.gameP2: A run is stored as its seed and the ordered list of your actions, not as a score. The server replays that list to compute the score, sprints, tickets delivered and commits, along with the start and end times.
privacy.gameP3: A submitted run that fails to replay is kept, marked rejected: it is the only record of what was sent.
privacy.publicP1: The leaderboard shows your display name, score, sprints, tickets delivered and the date of the run. Your email address appears nowhere.
privacy.publicP2: The display name is yours to choose: pick one you do not mind being public.
privacy.cookiesP1: The only cookies are authentication cookies: the session cookie, and very short-lived ones set while you sign in with Google. None of them tracks you, so there is no banner to click.
privacy.cookiesP2: Fonts are served by this site, not by a third party. No request goes out to an external service when a page loads.
privacy.thirdPartyP1: Three of them, and no more:
privacy.thirdPartyI1: The host, which runs the machine and the database.
privacy.thirdPartyI2: The service that delivers sign-in emails.
privacy.thirdPartyI3: Google, only if you choose to sign in with Google.
privacy.thirdPartyP2: Nothing is sold, rented or passed to anyone else.
privacy.retentionP1: Account data, the profile and the runs are kept as long as the account exists. No scheduled erasure job runs: nothing disappears after a set period.
privacy.retentionP2: Sessions stop being valid at their expiry date, and sign-in links after fifteen minutes.
privacy.rightsP1: You have the right to access, rectify, erase and port your data, and to object to its processing.
privacy.rightsP2: The display name can be changed from the Profile page. For anything else — a copy of your data, deleting the account — write to the contact address: there is no self-service button yet.
privacy.rightsP3: Deleting the account cascades to the profile and to every run; the matching rows leave the leaderboard with them.
privacy.rightsP4: If you disagree with how this is handled, you can complain to the CNIL (cnil.fr).
privacy.changesP1: This page can change. The date at the top is the latest version.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: What the service offers, what it does not promise, and the leaderboard rules.
terms.serviceP1: Devgame is a browser game: a roguelike whose dungeon is a Git graph. It plays without an account. An account stores your progress on the server and puts you on the leaderboard.
terms.serviceP2: Using the site means accepting these terms.
terms.freeP1: The service is free and provided as is. No availability is guaranteed: it can be interrupted, changed or shut down.
terms.freeP2: The game's rules change over time. When they do, runs played under the old rules stop being ranked: they still load, they are simply no longer comparable.
terms.freeP3: Keep your own backup if your progress matters to you: progress held in the browser goes when the site's data goes.
terms.accountI1: A valid email address you can read: that is how signing in works.
terms.accountI3: The display name is at most 24 characters. It must not impersonate another player, be abusive, or carry advertising.
terms.accountI4: You are answerable for what is done from your account.
terms.fairPlayP1: The score is never taken from the client. The server replays the action list you send and writes the score the engine computes. A run that does not replay is refused, and the submitted log is kept.
terms.fairPlayI1: Do not alter a run's log before sending it.
terms.fairPlayI3: Do not submit the same run twice: duplicates are detected and counted once.
terms.fairPlayI4: Stay within the submission rate limits.
terms.moderationP1: The publisher may remove a score, rename or hide a display name, suspend or delete an account, in case of cheating, abuse or unlawful content.
terms.moderationP2: A decision can be contested at the contact address in the legal notice.
terms.ipP1: The game, its code and its content remain the publisher's property. An account grants a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use them.
terms.ipP2: By submitting a run you accept that your display name and its result are shown on the leaderboard, which is public.
terms.liabilityP1: The service is free and comes with no warranty. The publisher is not liable for lost progress, for an interruption, or for indirect damages.
terms.liabilityP2: Nothing here excludes liability that the law does not allow to be excluded.
terms.dataP1: It is handled as described in the privacy policy.
terms.lawP1: French law applies. Failing an amicable settlement, disputes go to the competent French courts.
terms.changesP1: These terms can change. The date at the top is the version in force; playing on after a change means accepting it.
